body:
hollow-test mutates source files IN PLACE. Every restore path was process-local — the runner's `finally` and a single SIGINT handler — so a run that died mid-trial stranded a live mutant as an unstaged edit. The next run then refused with `commit or stash first`, which reads as if the USER's uncommitted work is in the way; the reflex is to commit it, and that is how a mutant ships.

Observed twice: a 10-minute agent tool timeout stranded `? 130 :` flipped to `? 131 :` in a plugin CLI, and an `authorized = false` -> `true` flip was stranded the same way earlier.

Measured before the fix, signalling a real run mid-trial: SIGINT restored cleanly (the only handled signal), while SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGKILL each stranded a mutant. SIGTERM is what `timeout(1)`, CI job cancellation, process supervisors and agent tool timeouts all send; SIGHUP is what closing a terminal sends. The one handled signal was the one automation never sends.

## What to build

Two layers, because neither is sufficient alone.

1. Handle every catchable termination signal — SIGTERM and SIGHUP restore exactly as SIGINT does. SIGKILL is deliberately excluded: it cannot be caught.
2. Write an on-disk in-flight record (the file plus its original bytes) before each mutation, and consume it on the NEXT run, restoring the file BEFORE the dirty-tree check rather than blaming the operator for the dirt. This is the only layer that survives SIGKILL, an OOM kill or a power loss.

The record must live in the git dir, so it is never committable and is per-worktree (`--git-dir` resolves to `.git/worktrees/<name>` in a linked worktree). A record whose owner pid is still alive must be left alone: that is a concurrent run, not a corpse, and restoring its file mid-trial would corrupt it and could report its mutant as killed. Probing that liveness must observe without disturbing the process.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run killed by SIGTERM mid-trial leaves no mutant in the working tree.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "SIGTERM mid-run restores" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
2. A run killed by SIGHUP mid-trial leaves no mutant in the working tree.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "SIGHUP mid-run restores" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
3. A mutant stranded by SIGKILL is restored by the next run, which reports it via a `recovered` field in `--json` instead of failing with the dirty-tree refusal.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "recovered by the next run" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
4. The in-flight record is written inside the git dir and is invisible to `git status`.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "in-flight record" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
5. A run that finishes normally removes its in-flight record, so nothing stale can be replayed.
   Verify: covered by the same `in-flight record` pattern above; exits 0.
6. A record owned by a LIVE pid is not restored, and probing that pid does not signal it.
   Verify: `node --test --test-name-pattern "live pid" packages/hollow-test/test/hollow-test.test.mjs` exits 0.
7. No surviving mutants in the changed code.
   Verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0.
8. No regression across the suite.
   Verify: `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` exits 0.

## Out of scope

The `adlc` dispatcher's failure to forward signals to the tool child is a separate defect with its own ticket and PR: invoked as `adlc hollow-test`, the signal never reaches this process at all, so even the SIGINT handler that worked was unreachable. Either fix alone leaves a gap.

Rails are deliberately empty. This ticket exists to change `packages/hollow-test/`, and `rail-freeze` unions rails across every incomplete ticket — declaring a rail on the files this ticket must edit would freeze them for every PR in the repo, including this one.
title: hollow-test must never leave a mutant in the working tree after an interrupt
